item.title: Your Gas Bill This Week: Iran, Hormuz, and What $4.14 Gas Does to the Fed
item.description:
The Strait of Hormuz is at a standstill — the IEA calls it the largest oil market disruption in history. Brent crude has surged 30% since the Iran conflict began, gas hit $4.14 a gallon this week, and the Cleveland Fed is now forecasting 3.9% headline PCE inflation. Marcus sees a transient shock with bypass options and Fed flexibility. James sees a structural inflation trap that kills rate cuts for 2026. One of them is right — and the answer changes what you do with your portfolio this week.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Pulse 03:00 — Segment 1 07:00 — Segment 2 14:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • IEA — Strait of Hormuz disruption is the largest in global oil market history • IEA — Oil prices risen 30% since Iran conflict outbreak; Brent at $95/barrel • BLS — U.S. CPI rose 3.3% year-over-year in March 2026, up from 2.4% prior month; energy prices up 12 • Cleveland Fed — Real-time inflation forecast: 3.9% headline PCE in Q1 2026, up from 2.7% pre-war • Dallas Fed scenario analysis — Hormuz closure of 1, 2, or 3 quarters adds 0.35, 0.79, or 1.47 percen
Next episode: If the ceasefire holds, does the Fed cut in June — or is the inflation damage already done?

item.title: Your Fed This Week: Why a Rate HIKE Is Back on the Table
item.description:
This week, prediction markets say 98% chance of no April Fed hike — but energy-driven inflation is quietly rewriting that calculus. Marcus and James debate whether the Fed's 'transitory' playbook holds up when Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack is openly warning inflation could hit 3.5% in April and the FOMC meets in just three weeks.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Pulse 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Polymarket — 98.3% implied probability of no Fed rate change at April 28-29, 2026 FOMC meeting • FRC prediction markets — 98.4% odds for no change, $13.7 million in volume on that outcome • FOMC March 18, 2026 projections — median federal funds rate 3.1% for 2026, central tendency 2.9-3.6% • March 2026 nonfarm payrolls — 178,000 job gain, unemployment at 4.3% • Yahoo Finance, April 7, 2026 — energy price shocks curbing Fed easing bets, speculation of 2026 rate

item.title: Your Tariffs This Week: Supreme Court Ruled — So Why Are They Still There?
item.description:
The Supreme Court struck down Trump's IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on February 20th — but this week, tariffs are still sitting at 10% and climbing. Marcus and James debate whether constitutional clarity is actually bullish for your portfolio, or whether the pivot to Section 122 just replaced one uncertainty with another. Plus: the $175 billion refund question nobody is talking about.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 05:00 — Segment 1 10:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump (Feb 20, 2026) — Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that IEEPA does not autho • Chief Justice John Roberts majority opinion — rejected presidential power to 'unilaterally impose un • Trump Executive Order Feb 20, 2026 — terminated IEEPA tariffs effective February 24, 2026 • Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 — Trump imposed 10% across-the-board tariffs effective February • Wharton Budget Model — projects up to $175 billion in potential refunds from invalidated IEEPA tarif
Next episode: Congress has 150 days to vote on extending Section 122. What happens to your portfolio if they don't?

item.title: Your Portfolio This Week: The AI-to-Utilities Rotation — Justified or Panic?
item.description:
Tech stocks are bleeding while utilities are surging — and this week the data is forcing investors to pick a side. Marcus makes the case that $2.9 trillion in data center construction makes this rotation a massive overreaction. James fires back: when 75% of companies still can't show AI ROI, the rotation isn't panic — it's pricing reality. Who's right? Your 401k is in the middle.

item.title: Your 401k This Week: Why the Fed's Tariff Silence Is Actually Bullish
